$comment: v3 REFUSAL VECTORS FROM CC CORPUS, copied verbatim. Five records, two shapes, both arms.
FOUR ARE LIFTED UNMODIFIED FROM THE RUNNING SERVICE on 9093: two out of the store and two
off GET /v1/refusals. The fifth is CONSTRUCTED and named so.
THE COMBINATION MATRIX, AND THE ONE CELL THAT DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE:
not-supplied        recorded, no note    recorded WITH note
store shape           served-not-supplied served-recorded      constructed-...  (built)
served shape          served-row-not-...  served-row-recorded  NONE
The empty cell is not an oversight. The live service never emits a served row on the
recorded arm carrying a note, because the ceiling refusal builds {state, limit, unit,
observed} and sets none. So that path is covered by PROJECTING the constructed store record
to the served shape and requiring CC Corpus's own signature to verify over it: a wrong
projection fails loudly rather than passing quietly. It is the one cell held by a
construction rather than by a record a deployment produced, and the gate says so on every
run rather than leaving it to be noticed.
IT CLOSES WHEN THE CEILING REFUSAL WRITES ITS NOTE. payment-host.ts:1352 already records the
fact such a note would carry: the effective ceiling may be the credential's figure or a
deployment's tighter one, and the two are indistinguishable at that point. That is the claim
S10 kept the field for. Writing it into the signed note makes this cell real. CC Corpus
recommends it; it needs a corpus regeneration and is Boyd's call.
ALL FIVE VERIFY AND ALL FIVE REJECT a one-unit change to the amount. Asserted, not assumed.
THESE ARE LOAD-BEARING IN A WAY TEST DATA USUALLY IS NOT. The parity gate compares this page
to npm latest, which is rc.12 and has no v3, so the v3 half is oracled entirely by these
records and not by the package. Until the pin moves past v3 they are the only thing between
a v3 record and a false negative on this page.
Under scripts/, which netlify.toml 404s, so this is not published.

refusals.reason: This payment moves 2887437 minor units (2 dp) of MXN and the mandate's per_transaction_ceiling is 25000 MXN, which is 2500000 at the same scale. The payment exceeds it and is refused. The constraint breached is `actionScope.per_transaction_ceiling`. This figure is the EFFECTIVE ceiling: a deployment may tighten it below what the credential declares and may never raise it, so compare against the credential to see whether it was tightened.

appliedBound.note: The ceiling applied is the EFFECTIVE one: a deployment may have tightened the credential figure, and at this point the two are indistinguishable.

refusals.reason: The attestation verified and its outcome, 'no_procede_reverso_abono', is not one this mandate treats as authorising a payment. Membership in the decider's declared vocabulary is checked elsewhere and is a different question: nothing in verification reads an outcome as permitting anything, so without this a requirement to cite a decision is satisfied by citing a signed DENIAL.

appliedBound.note: The mandate required a decision attestation; the one this payment cited verified, and its outcome is not one this mandate treats as authorising a payment. No spending bound was compared, because no mandate amount constraint was reached.
